title: Molecular Genetics
standard_text: The structure of DNA and the experiments that found it; DNA replication; transcription and translation; the genetic code; mutations; gene regulation; and genetic engineering and biotechnology. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 11 and 12: Science (2008), Biology, Grade 12, University Preparation (SBI4U), Strand D: Molecular Genetics)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Biology (SBI4U) worksheets on molecular genetics: DNA structure, replication, transcription, translation, the genetic code, mutations, gene regulation and biotechnology. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A pairs with T (U in RNA); G pairs with C.
body_html:
How to think about it

DNA is a double helix of nucleotides; the strands are antiparallel and held by hydrogen bonds between A–T and G–C. Replication is semi-conservative: helicase unwinds the helix and DNA polymerase builds new strands 5′ to 3′ (leading strand continuously, lagging strand in Okazaki fragments).

In transcription, RNA polymerase copies a gene into mRNA. In translation, ribosomes read the mRNA in codons of three bases and tRNA brings the matching amino acids. Mutations change the base sequence: a substitution may change one amino acid, while an insertion or deletion shifts the reading frame.

Example

DNA strand: 3′-TAC GGA-5′. mRNA?

Pair each base; U replaces T.

Answer: 5′-AUG CCU-3′

Example

A DNA sample is 30% A. What percent is G?

T = 30%, so A + T = 60%

G + C = 40%, G = 20%

Answer: 20%

Common mistakes

  • Pairing A with U in DNA.
  • Forgetting that the two strands run in opposite directions.
  • Thinking every mutation is harmful: many are silent.

items.q: In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 20% of the bases are adenine (A). What percentage are thymine (T)?
items.e: A pairs with T, so T = 20%. A + T = 40%, so G + C = 60% and G = C = 30%.

items.q: In the DNA of a fungus, 37% of the bases are adenine. What percentage are cytosine?
items.e: A + T = 74%, so G + C = 26%, and cytosine = half of that: 13.0%.

items.e: A pairs with T, so T = 32%. A + T = 64%, so G + C = 36% and G = C = 18%.

Each PCR cycle takes 2 minutes. How many cycles can be completed in 20 minutes, and so how many times larger is the DNA amount?
items.e: 10 cycles; amount × 210 = 1024.

items.q: A linear DNA molecule of 4000 base pairs is cut by a restriction enzyme at positions 300, 2700, 3550. Which fragment sizes (bp) appear on the gel?
items.e: Subtract neighbouring positions (including 0 and 4000): 2400, 850, 450, 300. The smallest fragments move furthest on the gel.

items.q: A linear DNA molecule of 2400 base pairs is cut by a restriction enzyme at positions 1250. Which fragment sizes (bp) appear on the gel?
items.e: Subtract neighbouring positions (including 0 and 2400): 1250, 1150. The smallest fragments move furthest on the gel.

items.q: A linear DNA molecule of 2400 base pairs is cut by a restriction enzyme at positions 1250, 1500, 2250. Which fragment sizes (bp) appear on the gel?
items.e: Subtract neighbouring positions (including 0 and 2400): 1250, 750, 250, 150. The smallest fragments move furthest on the gel.

items.q: What is needed for PCR?
c: DNA, primers, free nucleotides and Taq DNA polymerase
items.e: A thermal cycler changes the temperature.

items.q: PCR starts with 20 DNA molecules. How many molecules are there after 20 cycles?
items.e: The DNA doubles each cycle: 20 × 220 = 2.10 × 107.
